subtopics.title: Income — Gross, Deductions and What Actually Arrives

questions.question: Gross salary is R10 500,00 and the deductions are R840,00, R105,00 and R525,00. The net income is:
The pension contribution is five percent of gross salary. Is the R525,00 on the payslip consistent with that?
options: No — five percent of R10 500 is R210,00
No — five percent of R10 500 is R1 050,00
It cannot be checked without the pension fund's rules

questions.question: Why may the deductions NOT appear again in the household's list of expenses?
options: Because they are smaller than the other expenses
Because they never reached the household, so listing them again subtracts the same money twice
Because they are occasional costs, not monthly ones
Because only SARS may record them

questions.question: Total household income is the net salary plus R1 100,00 rent received plus R1 070,00 from Saturday hair work. That total is:
Which of these is a FIXED expense in the household budget?
Prepaid electricity is bought every single month, yet it is classified as variable. Why?
options: Because it is paid in cash
Because the municipality sets the price
Because the amount changes with how much is used
Because it is cheaper than rent

questions.question: Putting aside R350,00 every month for January's school uniforms is called:
The variable expenses are R2 750, R820, R940, R260 and R330. Their total is:

subtopics.title: The Budget and Its Bottom Line

questions.question: Income is R11 200,00 and expenditure is R10 259,00. The bottom line is:
How does a budget differ from an income and expenditure statement?
options: A budget covers a year; a statement covers a month
A budget is a plan drawn up before the period; a statement records what actually happened afterwards
A budget uses gross income; a statement uses net income
They are two names for the same document

questions.question: Rent of R3 400,00 out of income of R11 200,00 is approximately:
If the R1 070,00 hair income stops, which items should be adjusted first, and why?
options: The fixed items, because they are the largest amounts
The deductions, because they come off first
The variable items, because they are the only amounts that can be changed within the month
The rent, because housing is a luxury

subtopics.title: Break-Even — When the Stall Starts Making Money

questions.question: A koeksister sells for R6,50 and costs R2,80 to make. Each sale contributes how much towards the fixed costs?
With fixed costs of R720,00, the break-even number of koeksisters per month is:
Why is the break-even figure of 194,59 rounded UP rather than down?
options: Because 194 sales still leave a loss of R2,20, while 195 give a profit of R1,50
Because money answers always round up
Because the fixed costs are a round number
Because decimals are not allowed in Mathematical Literacy

questions.question: Selling 360 koeksisters in a month, the stall's profit is:

subtopics.title: Money That Walks In, Money That Walks Out

questions.question: Which figure belongs on the Simplifier's "in" envelope?
options: The R10 500 printed at the top of the payslip
The R9 030 that actually lands in the bank, plus any other money received
The total of the month's accounts

questions.question: The UIF contribution is described as:
options: five rand for every hundred you earn
a flat R525 for every worker
one rand for every hundred you earn

questions.question: Why does the Simplifier warn against treating the R1 070 hair money like a salary?
options: Because it is taxed at a higher rate
Because it is a fixed cost
Because it is too small to matter
Because it came last month and may not come this month, so a careful household budgets on the money it can rely on

subtopics.title: The Bills That Don't Care How Your Month Went

questions.question: Which question does the Simplifier say classifies any bill correctly?
options: Does the amount change when I change what I do?
Is it paid by debit order?

questions.question: Why are the variable bills "the first place to look when money runs short"?
options: Because they are always the biggest
Because they are the only part of the out-envelope that can move within the month
Because they are paid last in the month

questions.question: How does the household prepare for December and January's uniforms?
options: By borrowing when those months arrive
By treating them as fixed monthly contracts
By leaving them out of the budget
By paying them in slices in advance — R450 and R350 a month put aside

subtopics.title: The Koeksisters That Pay for the Table

questions.question: Rent takes R3 400 and groceries R2 750 out of R11 200. What does the Simplifier conclude?
options: That the budget is in deficit
That the roof and the food together swallow more than half of everything the family earns
That groceries should be cut to zero
That rent is a variable cost

questions.question: What does a deficit always require?
options: Somebody to pay for it — savings, a loan, or an account left unpaid

questions.question: Selling 360 koeksisters, income is R2 340,00 and total cost is R1 728,00. What remains?
What does the Simplifier say every bottom line must be followed by?
options: A second calculation as a check
One plain sentence saying what the household or stall should actually do next
